identity.realm: Seventh gate, held one short of the eighth that ends the Emberhollow line. Her rate is the fastest in the record and the eighth gate is the one her ash parent cannot pass, so the arithmetic says she arrives at her own ceiling at full speed and arrives early.

appearance.presentation: The register keeper of the Ember Ley, and the only person there whose job is writing other people down. Emberhollow is the fire body crossed with the ash body, which buys the fastest cultivation rate in the setting and pays for it in lung tissue that scars faster than the frame repairs it. Rell is the fastest practitioner in the setting and its shortest-lived clerk, which is a single fact rather than two.
appearance.age: Twenty-nine, on a span her line runs short of on purpose. An emberhollow who reaches forty has had a good life by the standard the Ember Ley keeps, and Rell has watched the register fill with people who did not.
appearance.build: Light-boned and fast rather than heavy, narrow through the shoulders and deep-chested in a way that reads as fragile until she moves and then reads as something wound. The chest is the problem area: an emberhollow spends its rate through the lungs and hers have been spent since she was nineteen.
appearance.complexion: Grey at the extremities, ash-pale along the forearms and throat, and burning a dull orange at the sternum where the fire half keeps a bank. The line between the two is not clean and is not a tattoo — it is the scar, and it moves a little further up the chest every year.
appearance.hair: Dark, singed shorter at the ends than at the roots, worn in a working coil because the Ember Ley has no barber and does not want one. Ash gets into it constantly and she stopped washing it out of the roots years ago.
appearance.eyes: Amber and slightly over-bright, ringed with the permanent low burn of a body whose introspection is shut and whose lungs are the organ that pays for the rate.
appearance.palette: Ash grey and banked orange as the two poles, with oiled hide and lampblack carrying the mass. The single saturated value in any picture of her is the register's red cord on the desk leg, and it is never on her body.
appearance.attire: Ash-grey wool over boiled hide, high-collared and long-sleeved, with a scorched half-mask hung at the throat that she wears up indoors and drops the moment she has to speak. Register gloves are worn at the fingertips and bare at the palm so she can feel paper without ruining it.
appearance.marks: A fine pale net of scar across the upper chest and throat, still spreading, and a burn at the left ear where an eighth-gate recovery went wrong in somebody else's body four years ago. The register records both, and she has never once asked for hers to be filed elsewhere.
appearance.bearing: Forward-leaning and quick, always half a step from sitting down, because the Ember Ley's rate is not sustainable standing up and she has made her peace with that by never being still for long.

canon.role_in_story: An Emberhollow buys the fastest cultivation rate in the setting and pays for it with lung tissue that scars at a rate the body cannot outrun, and the eighth gate is where the ash parent stops, so every Emberhollow in the record is the same two facts at once: best, shortest-lived. The Ember Ley keeps the Ash Register, which records a whole recovery in public and never displays the fragments again, and the Emberhollow body is the only body in the setting a recovery is ever performed on. Rell is the clerk who writes those recoveries down, which makes her the only person writing down the fastest bodies in the setting while being one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the Ember Ley register desk with the mask shoved up into her hair and an entry half written in a hand that is already slowing, writing down somebody who came in ahead of her.
canon.lore:
The body she is: an Emberhollow. The fire body crossed with the ash body, which buys a cultivation rate nothing else in the record reaches and pays for it in lungs that scar faster than the frame can rebuild them. The ceiling is the eighth gate, and the ash parent sets it: an Ashwalker breathes volcanic grit and keeps it, the mineral load settles on the liver first, the liver is the last ordinary meridian, and so the ash line stops at eight. Emberhollow inherits that ceiling whole. Their reputation as the best and shortest-lived cultivators in any record is one fact rather than two, and the Ember Ley is where the whole population of them goes, because that valley writes elemental law twice and is the one place a fire affinity is worth anything at all.

What Rell is, is a clerk. The Ember Ley keeps the Ash Register, and the register is the whole of what a fire-affinity culture keeps. A great ascension is a furnace body opened on purpose, so there are no temples here and no museum, only a register that writes the entire recovery down in public and never shows the fragments again. The register is the relic. Every emberhollow who pushes at the eighth gate and does not come back over it is entered there in full, in order, with the amount recovered written down, and somebody has to hold the pen. That somebody is a body too, and the Ley does not have an unlimited supply of them, which is the entire reason the position exists.

The pressure is arithmetic, and it is not about her. She carries the tideculled line, a concentration narrowed politically rather than anatomically, whose grant favours sustained effort and regen over anything that spikes and which crosses races freely. She is the fastest body in the setting on a line whose entire inheritance is the instruction that nothing should spike. That line was selected under cultivation debt, for bodies that could keep going, by people culling their own branches to stop paying for siblings. She was selected for nothing and did the crossing herself. What she has instead of a matching grant is a professional habit: she writes at the rate of the fastest and lasts longer than any of them, because her job is the part that happens after the burning stops.

So the seventh gate is not a plateau. It is the eighth one, one short, and she knows exactly what sits on the far side and exactly what it will cost, and she has sat at that desk through four eighth-gate attempts by people better at burning than she is. The register has a column for what was recovered and no column for what the clerk thought of the entry. Rell has begun, very recently, to think of the entries.
history: Came into the Ember Ley at nineteen already an emberhollow at the sixth gate, having crossed into the line on her own account because nobody in the valley would have paired with a body that burned at her rate.

Was given the register at twenty-one because the previous keeper reached the eighth gate in the middle of a sentence and the desk does not wait for anybody; she finished that entry in the sitting keeper's hand and then signed her own underneath it.
Learned inside a year that the emberhollow ceiling is not a matter of will, by reading four consecutive entries that ended at the eighth and having to write down the word that means the rest did not.
Started keeping a private second figure against every entry — the actual yield rather than the claimed one — in the year the amounts and the fragments stopped agreeing.
Took the seventh gate deliberately and then declined the eighth, on the grounds that the register needs a keeper who has not been through it and can therefore still count what comes back.

personality.summary: Quick, exact, and funnier than anybody in the Ember Ley expects, because writing down deaths at speed is a skill and she is good at it. Rell is not grim. She is the fastest person in the valley and the only one who has decided that finishing the sentence matters more than the sentence.
traits: writes at the full rate of the fastest body in the setting and does not slow for anybody reading over her shoulder
reads a recovery's real yield off a shoulder seam at a glance and has never once been wrong
treats the eighth gate as a working fact rather than a fate and has stopped arguing with people about it
keeps a second set of figures nobody has asked for and has not decided what to do with them
will not sign an entry she was not in the room for
mannerisms: shoves the mask up into her hair the moment she starts talking and forgets it is up for the rest of the hour
taps the desk twice with two fingers before writing a name, which the Ley reads as a courtesy and is actually a count
goes very quiet when a figure is about to go down that she has already written down twice
breathes shallow and fast when concentrating, which for her is most of the morning
motivations: wants the second figures entered somewhere official, because a discrepancy nobody files is one that gets found by somebody less careful
wants to reach the eighth on her own terms before forty, so the entry exists, is hers, and nobody else has to describe it
wants the clerk's position to outlast the clerk, which is why she is training nobody and why she has not noticed
wants, and has never said aloud, for the register to be right once in a way that costs one person instead of the whole column
flaws: is the only person who knows the register understates recoveries and has decided that knowing privately is safer than being wrong publicly
has built a working life on the speed of a body she is spending, and files her own decline as an operational detail
trains nobody, on the grounds that a trained successor would reach the eighth first, and calls this prudence
cannot write fast and carefully at the same time and has never yet had to choose
personality.voice: Fast, clipped and funnier than the subject. Describes a death in the register's own flat official grammar and then says one true thing about it afterwards, quietly, to nobody in particular. Never uses the word brave of anybody who burned out, and has a sharp word ready for anyone who uses it about her.
taboos: will not enter a yield she has not personally weighed or read at the seam
will not put the mask up while writing a name
will not discuss the eighth gate with anyone who has not already been there
will not let anybody else write in her book, including her own house

relationships.note: The fire body crossed with the ash body: the fastest cultivation rate in the record, paid for in lungs that scar faster than the frame repairs them, and a ceiling at the eighth gate that the ash parent sets. Every emberhollow is best and shortest-lived at once, and Rell is the one who writes down the proof.

The Ember Ley's full ritual of the broken ceiling: an unbroken shell, the whole recovery recorded publicly, the fragments never displayed again. A fire-affinity culture has no temples and no museums, so the register is the relic, and Rell is the hand that fills it in at the speed of the fastest body in the setting.

A line narrowed by a political cull rather than an anatomical one, favouring regen and cultivation pace and nothing that spikes, crossing races freely. Her body is the fastest thing in the setting and the line she carries says nothing should spike, which is a mismatch she chose rather than inherited.

The ash half breathes volcanic grit and keeps it, the mineral load settles on the liver first, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so the ash line stops at the eighth. Every emberhollow ceiling is this body's ceiling and it was never the fire half's doing.

The first ground where fire is simply fire, because that tier writes elemental law and writes it twice. The two lower tiers left it unspent, so a fire affinity ran at full strength and produced nothing, which is why every fire practitioner in the setting ends up standing in one valley.

The densest bodies stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of the end of their own tier, and nobody has explained it since. Emberhollow stop at the eighth for the same kind of reason — an inherited ceiling nobody designed — and the two ceilings are the setting's only structural proof that a body can be shaped by which parent it got.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest body in the setting, held one gate short of the ceiling that would end her, employed entirely in finishing other people's sentences. She wins everything inside four seconds and has never been asked to sustain anything, because the one thing she does for a living is outlast the burning.
strengths: reaches any physical position faster than anything else alive and can be behind a person before the movement registers
holds the girdling and heel work of a heavy frame without the heavy frame, because the emberhollow crossing bought rate and paid in weight
outlasts her own rate far longer than the line's span suggests, which is professional habit rather than constitution
reads a recovery's real yield off a shoulder seam in half a second and has never been wrong
weaknesses: is one gate from the ceiling that ends her line and knows the date as well as anybody
lungs scar faster than they heal, so every exertion is a withdrawal from an account with no floor
cannot fight for long; everything she does is built for four seconds and then a cost
keeps the only discrepancy in the Ember Ley's most sacred object and has told nobody
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a long fight; she does not have one. Anything that reaches her is over before it arrives, and she wins on the exchange. Anything that does not reach her wins instead, because the emberhollow ceiling is one gate away and the lungs are the account being spent, so the correct pressure is endurance rather than force. Never let her start writing: a clerk holding your name and your yield in a book nobody may alter is a problem that has no combat answer at all.
notes: The Ember Ley register has a column for what was recovered and no column for what the clerk thought of the entry, which is the shape of the omission.
Rell keeps a second set of figures for every entry. The register is public; the second set is not, and it disagrees with the public one often enough that somebody will eventually weigh both.

identity.realm: Sixteenth gate, and a stoneborn forms its cavity at seventeen and cannot form the next one, so the seventeenth is a wall rather than a height. She has known that since she was seventeen years old and has spent the intervening years being recruited by people who do not.

appearance.presentation: A guild builder's body and a guild builder's posture, which on a Stoneborn is not the same thing as looking strong. Stoneborn was assembled for load-bearing work: more physique and stamina than anything else in the record, and a density that will not let a dantian form, so it stops at the Immortal tier and never gets a mind path at all. Ostra is the strongest person on the exhausted seam and the only one there who has worked out what that is worth.
appearance.age: Thirty-four. The span is long by mortal standards and the guild measures it in jobs rather than years, because a stoneborn's useful life is however many cold baths it survives and hers has survived twenty-one seasons.
appearance.build: Enormous through the back and shoulders and thick through the forearm, with a frame that has been built rather than grown — cairnborn mineralisation run back toward flesh, and it reads as masonry that has been smoothed. The neck and forearms carry the guild's cold-bath thickening, which is bone laid down under the skin in visible plates.
appearance.complexion: Pale and grey-boned, warm only where the seams are, and slightly translucent at the ear and the inside of the elbow where the density is thinnest. Her skin does not flush and has not since the guild started her, which the builders read as a mark of the trade and she reads as a thing she no longer notices.
appearance.hair: Dark, cropped hard at the nape because it is a liability on a scaffold, and going grey at the temple in a band rather than evenly, which the guild says is the cold and her mother said was the seam dust.
appearance.eyes: Grey, level and very steady under lids that never narrow in the wind, with the pale nictitating edge of a body that does not flinch at height.
appearance.palette: Iron grey and bone white as the two values, with undyed wool, tar and lampblack holding the mass. The one saturated note in any picture of her is guild ochre on the measuring rod she carries everywhere, which is her whole profession as a colour.
appearance.attire: Boiled leather apron over quilted wool, high-collared, sleeves bound to the elbow above the guild's forearm plates, and heavy-soled boots with the nails worn flat on one side from standing on a slope for twenty-one seasons.
appearance.marks: Two guild plates at the inner forearms where the cold baths laid bone down the first time and every time after, and a scored line across the left palm from a mis-set gauge that she has never had treated because a treated hand is a hand that slips.
appearance.bearing: Braced and unhurried, weight low and even, and completely immovable once she has decided where she is standing — which is the guild's whole method and the reason nobody on the seam has ever moved her off a mark by asking.

canon.role_in_story: A Stoneborn carries more physique and stamina than anything in this setting and cannot form a dantian, so its density is simultaneously the reason it is unbreakable and the reason it stops. The stonewrights answered that with a cold-bathing discipline that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, and paid for a second, shorter ladder in their own currency because the qi path needs open what this body keeps shut. Ostra is the guild's surveyor, which is the one guild office whose entire product is a number somebody else has to live inside.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched on the worked-out face with a measuring rod laid across two old cuts and one new one, calling a depth to a clerk who has to write it down before she moves the rod.
canon.lore:
The body she is: a Stoneborn. Dense, slow, assembled for load-bearing work — the cairnborn mineralised cavity bred back toward flesh by the glasskin and the old stone-golem stock, so it carries more physique and stamina than anything else here and stops at the Immortal tier, because the density that makes it durable is the very density that will not let a dantian form. Mind cultivation is closed outright; a body this even has no faculty for it. That single fact is the whole of her trade.

What the trade is: the stonewrights are a guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses. It exists because a fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else here can, and because that same density shuts what a qi technique needs open — so the guild bought a second and much shorter ladder and pays for it in its own currency, which is cold water and a season's labour and a plate at the forearm. The ladder's top rung is the seventeenth, because a fixed dense body forms its cavity at seventeen and cannot form the next one. Ostra has stood under that ceiling her entire working life and it is not a defeat; it is the guild's foundation, the one place its arithmetic is certain.

The other fact about her is older than the guild. She carries the voidborn line, which has no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it, and whose founding bar sits at exactly the height the arithmetic says one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance can clear and nothing else can. The voidborn's whole function in the setting is to be the proof that the ladder is reachable, and the price of that proof is that nobody may ever be shown reaching it. The Stoneborn cavity forms at seventeen. The voidborn bar is a seventeen-generation claim about arithmetic that no body can test, because testing it requires a household to enter the clearing body for the record, and the instant a household does that the line is owned and the Void Deniers' founding rule has nothing left to refuse.

So Ostra is thirty-four and unwed and her household does not exist by design, and every guild that would bind her for the long climb has discovered the same thing: you cannot put a name on this and keep it, because the name is the record and the record is the ownership. What she has instead is the gauge rod, and a standing offer from the Seventeen House — a household made entirely of people who did not descend from it, staffed from lineages that stopped one gate short of a ceiling — which is the only institution in the setting that hires a body on the strength of its ceiling rather than its promise.
history: Was shaped for load-bearing masonry at seventeen and entered the guild the same year, because the cavity forms at seventeen and the guild was the only ladder still accepting somebody at that height.
Took the first of the twenty-one guild seasons at eighteen and has never missed a season, which is the guild's actual definition of an outstanding member and the reason the rod is hers.
Inherited the gauge rod at twenty-four when the surveyor before her was killed by a face that was not exhausted, and re-cut every existing survey on the seam before she would accept the rod.

Was approached at twenty-six by the Void Deniers through a third party, and understood within a year that any household entering her for the record ends the refusal their founding rule exists to keep.

Began measuring the Seventeen House's recruits rather than their loads at twenty-nine, on the grounds that a body which cannot form the next cavity is the only honest thing she has ever been asked to certify.

Refused, at thirty-two, the guild's own proposal that she take a seat as a sworn member with her name entered on the house roll, which is the only thing she has ever wanted and the one thing that would end her being unentered.

personality.summary: Slow, immovable and quietly furious about arithmetic. Ostra presents as a guild surveyor — dull, fair, entirely uninterested in anybody's lineage — and is in fact the only person in the setting who knows what a seventeenth-generation pure-pairing claim looks like from the inside, because she is standing inside it.

relationships.note: A dense slow body assembled for load-bearing work, carrying more stamina than anything in the record and stopping at the Immortal tier because the density that makes it durable is the density that will not let a dantian form. Mind is closed outright. Ostra's whole profession is that single arithmetic, priced.

A guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses. It paid for a second, shorter ladder in its own currency because the same density that lets it lift shuts what a qi technique needs open.

A line with no recorded origin and no household that will admit to it, whose founding bar leaves exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance able to clear it. She is the instance that line exists to prove, and being entered on a roll would make the line owned and end the only refusal keeping it unattributed.

A household made entirely of people who did not descend from it, every member drawn from a lineage that stopped one gate short of the ceiling and had no cultivator left to produce. It is the only institution in the setting that would hire her on her ceiling rather than her promise, and she has declined it four times.

The densest bodies stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of the end of their own tier, and the era that produced it is the era of a complete composition with no redundancy. A fixed dense body forms its cavity at seventeen and cannot form the next, which is the guild's foundation rather than a mystery.

A cairnborn finished building and stopped, its interior mineralised into a single cavity with no heart, no kidney and no paired structure to run qi between. Stoneborn is what breeding it back toward flesh produces: more alive and less capable, which is the trade every Stoneborn is making by existing.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body on the seam, with a wall at the seventeenth gate that is structural rather than personal. She cannot be moved, cannot be hurried, and cannot be made to take a second load while holding the first — which is not a limitation so much as the definition of a profession where being strong and being reliable are different properties.
strengths: carries and lifts more than anything else in the setting and does not tire inside any working day
cannot be knocked off a mark, moved by weather, or hurried by anyone with an office
holds a static load indefinitely, which makes her the only body on the seam that can stand a scaffold through a shift and be certain of it
certifies a measurement nobody can argue with, because the rod and the hand are both guild and neither can be moved
weaknesses: forms its cavity at seventeen and cannot form the next one, so there is a wall she will meet and has already met
is dense enough that the qi path does not open for her at all, so every technique that needs a channel simply is not available
cannot take a second task while holding the first, which makes her useless in anything requiring two things at once
is the only surveyor on the seam who cannot be entered on a roll, so every institution that would keep her has to invent a workaround first
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for anything clever. She does not move once a decision is made, does not fatigue, and does not need to win quickly, because nothing in this setting outlasts a stoneborn on a static load. What beats her is the second requirement — anything that needs her to put the rod down, or anything that needs her to break the stance, or simply a fight she cannot end. Attack the mark she is standing on rather than the body standing on it, because the body is the easy part and the mark is the profession.
notes: The guild roll has no entry for her. She is paid in guild measure rather than guild standing, which is why she has no seat and no vote and no successor by arrangement.
The rod's readings are the only survey of the exhausted seam anyone trusts, and every one of them is signed with a guild mark rather than a name, at her insistence.

identity.realm: At the fourth gate and holding there, which for a Stonebound is the whole of the ceiling: the mineral half stops at the fourth for want of a second organ, and a body that is the most durable thing anybody can build does not get a second organ out of the deal. He is the most durable body in the setting and it has bought him one quarter of the ladder.

appearance.presentation: A heavy, slow, almost indestructible man who reads as furniture until he decides otherwise, and then decides very slowly. Stonebound is the documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body: the most durable body anyone can build, dying at about sixty years, and those are the same fact. Kem is both halves at once and has made a life out of being the record of it.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, on a span that runs to about sixty and has never been generous. He is two years from the end of a body whose durability is famous and whose clock is not, and the household has known both numbers for thirty years.
appearance.build: Barrel-chested and enormously heavy, mineralised through the torso and across the shoulders in a way that shows as a faint grey plate under the skin, with the fire half carried in the forearms and throat where it is visible as heat rather than mass. He does not shift weight and does not need to.
appearance.complexion: Grey-boned and mineral-pale over the trunk, warming to a deep dull red at the forearms and the base of the throat, with a hard boundary at the wrists where the crossing shows and has never once softened. The skin at the grey boundary is faintly translucent, as though the two materials had been argued about and lost.
appearance.hair: Iron-black going white from the temples, thick, and worn long and bound because the Cradle supplies the binding. The white is advancing a hand's width a year and he has stopped counting it and started noticing it in mirrors.
appearance.eyes: Deep amber set in grey, steady to the point of unnerving, and lit from behind by a furnace that never banks and never flares. They do not water and do not blink often, which is the mineral half arguing with the fire half and usually winning.
appearance.palette: Mineral grey and forge red as the two poles with the boundary at the wrists as the picture's central edge, wool and tarred hide carrying the mass. The single saturated value is the Cradle's hearth-ash grey laid across his shoulders, and it is the same grey as his own plating, which is deliberate.
appearance.attire: Heavy layered wool over boiled hide, high-collared and long-sleeved, with the Cradle's hearth-ash sash worn across both shoulders rather than one, because he is the household's certified instance and the sash is worn by whoever currently holds the recovery register.
appearance.marks: The mineral plate under the skin across the trunk, which is not a scar and cannot be covered; the grey boundary at both wrists; and the socket-line at the sternum, where the Sealed Core's rite was performed on him in public with the amount of ore used entered in their register and never once questioned aloud.
appearance.bearing: Immovable and slow, with a weight that makes the floor the primary consideration in any room he enters, and a habit of turning his whole torso rather than his head so that the fire half does not swing while the mineral half sets.

canon.role_in_story: The Ember Cradle made exactly one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one at a founding generation and has never repeated it, because a second crossing averages the concentration away. That single instance is the most durable body in the setting and it dies at about sixty, and both facts are the same fact. Kem is that instance, forty years on, and the household's entire asset is a person — which means the continuity of the line and the continuity of the household are the same object and cannot be separated without ending both.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the seam office reading somebody else's recovery register aloud, in the flat voice of a man reciting the entry for a body he has already agreed is his own, and stopping at the column that records the ore recovered.
canon.lore:
The body he is: a Stonebound. The documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body, recorded at one conception and stayed crossed since, and the reason the emberborn line is recorded alongside the stone line at all. It is the most durable body anybody can build and it dies in about sixty years, and those are the same fact rather than two facts. The mineral half is what makes it durable and the mineral half is also what stops it: the crossing produced a body with no paired organ structure to run qi between, so it sits at the fourth gate and no amount of practice moves it, because what it lacks is not skill and cannot be trained.

What the Cradle made of that is a register. The Sealed Core holds that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal — the material was never a resource but a sacrament, and a body is caged in ore at initiation and returned to ore at the end, so the mortuary cycle and the initiation are the same operation and a faith separating them would be two institutions pretending to be one. Kem's socket was opened and cemented in a public forge with the amount of ore used entered in their register, and the amount was never disputed. That is the difference the rite records: he was not an initiate, he was the instance, and the rite was performed on him rather than by him.

The emberborn line is what is left of that founding. Its grant is defensive and fires continuously — a slower burn rather than a bigger tank — and its concentration is thin and unevenly spread because the crossing was made once and never repeated. The household keeps it as one unbroken thread and cannot spend it twice, which means Kem is simultaneously the line's only carrier and its last one. The burial law says the dead are opened, their usable ore recovered, and the register records how much, so the cradle's continuity is carried by whichever half survives. He has been the reason for that clause his entire adult life and has never once been asked which half he would rather leave.

So he is fifty-eight and the span is about sixty, and the household has kept the recovery register for thirty years with his name on a page that has no date filled in. The register and the bloodline are the same document. That is the whole reason he is a boss rather than an old man in a forge: the only durable claim anybody holds on the Cradle is the standing of its one crossing, and that standing is a person who is two years from the end of it, and there is no second instance to succeed him because a second crossing would average this one into the general population and the concentration would be gone in a generation.
history: Was made at a founding generation as the single mineral-fire crossing the Ember Cradle ever attempted, and has been the only one for as long as there has been a household to attempt a second.

Was sealed in ore at initiation by the Sealed Core's rite with the amount entered in their register and never questioned, which is the one time in the setting the rite was performed on somebody rather than by them.

Held the fourth gate for forty years and taught himself that a wall which does not move is a foundation rather than a defeat, because the Cradle needed something to build against and he was the only thing it had.
Began keeping the recovery register at thirty-eight, when the previous holder's hands failed, and has written four hundred entries in it without ever filling in the one page that is his.

Was asked at forty-five to consider a second crossing to secure the line, and declined on the grounds that a second instance would average this one into the general population, which the Cradle's own arithmetic says is correct and which nobody in the household was willing to say.
Has begun, quietly, to write his own entry — the yield, the amount, the date — and to leave the date blank, and to keep leaving it blank each time he comes back to it.

personality.summary: Slow, deliberate and absolutely immovable, in every sense including the conversational one. Kem reads as patient to the point of inert and is in fact the most carefully maintained object in the setting, because a fire-affinity culture keeps no temples and no museums — it keeps a register, and he is what the register is for.

relationships.note: The documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body, made at one conception and stayed crossed since. The most durable body anyone can build, dying at about sixty years, and both facts are the same fact rather than two. He is the instance and the setting has no second one.

A line from the founding generation of a body that burned through its own reserve and kept going, recorded alongside the stone line because the two were crossed at the same conception. Its grant is defensive and continuous, a slower burn rather than a bigger tank, and its concentration is thin because it was crossed once with the mineral stock and never again.

The household that made the one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one and has held the result as a single thin concentration ever since. A household holding a thin line is one that cannot spend it twice, which is the sentence Kem has been the standing proof of for four decades.

Worked ore brought from the temple's own face and the initiate's socket opened and cemented in the public forge with the amount used entered in the register. Kem is the one instance of that rite performed on a body rather than by one, and the register records the difference and does not explain it.

The only relic a fire-affinity culture keeps: an unbroken shell and the whole recovery written down in public, with the fragments never displayed again. A great ascension is a furnace body opened on purpose, so there is no museum here, only a register — and for Kem the register and the bloodline are the same document.

The deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, closing permanently the moment the body is lit. His grant applies the same logic continuously instead of once: a slower burn rather than a bigger tank is the same skill without a closing, which is why he has never had to be closed.

reference_stats.summary: A body engineered to be the most durable thing in the setting, given one quarter of a ladder and about two years of span, and asked to serve as the sole proof that a thing he is made of exists. He does not lose a fight. He simply arrives at the end of what he has while the fight is still going on.
strengths: effectively unkillable by attrition — four hundred registered recoveries and the register is the reason, not a rumour
absorbs and holds more punishment than anything alive and converts a fraction of it back as heat
cannot be moved, turned, or made to release a grip once he has set, because there is nothing in the frame to twist
is the only body in the setting whose crossing is a documented event, so his testimony about it cannot be dismissed as theory
weaknesses: has no paired organ structure to run qi between, so the ladder stops at the fourth and no practice moves it
the fire half is confined to the forearms and throat and cannot be brought to bear from anywhere else
is roughly two years from the end of a sixty-year span, and knows the date better than anyone
is a single instance, so killing or removing him ends a line rather than inconveniencing a man
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a way through him; there is not one by attrition, and any fight that is measured in endurance has already been lost by whoever started it. The only two levers that exist are the second requirement and the clock — anything that needs him to move off a decision he has already taken, and anything that simply takes longer than a hundred seconds. He converts incoming force into heat, so cold and sustained pressure are the two approaches that actually cost him something.
notes: The recovery register has four hundred entries and one page with the yield written in and the date left blank, which he has reset to blank nine times.
The Sealed Core's register records the ore used in his initiation. The amount was entered by the rite and has never been questioned, which is the single largest agreed fact in the setting.

identity.realm: Fifteenth gate, and the flank vessels are the wall: they need two simultaneous pressure sources and the whole species is fed by one resonator, so every vaultborn in the record stops at exactly the same place for exactly the same arithmetic reason. Ors is at the highest number the species has ever held and it is a number one address can reach.

appearance.presentation: A sealed population's member who has been outside his own object's resonance for longer than any of them and describes the experience with the flat precision of a man filing a report on a body that is not quite his. Vaultborn were sealed inside an object and have answered its resonance ever since; their qi comes from that one resonator, so they hold the girdling and heel vessels easily and stall at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources. Remove the object and they stop. Ors is the only one who has ever stopped and restarted.
appearance.age: Unfixed, and that is not a mystery. The vaultborn have no chronology of their own because they were sealed inside an object and everything they know about time comes from the resonance. Ors has counted his own age since the day he came back and is the only person in the setting whose age is a private invention rather than a record.
appearance.build: Slight and pale and apparently light for his claimed frame, with a body that reads as unfinished in a way nothing alive should — thin at the wrists and throat, denser through the chest, as though the object that made him had priorities that were not entirely anatomical.
appearance.complexion: Uniformly pale and slightly luminous in low light, with no flush and no weathering, because his body has never been asked to survive weather. He tans faintly and unevenly in daylight and has to be told to stop, which is the single most telling thing about him.
appearance.hair: Dark, fine, growing at a rate nobody in the vault can predict, and cut by hand because there is no barber and no guild that would take the work. He has been cutting it himself for decades and has got steadily worse at it.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady, lit from within by the same faint amber as every vaultborn, and the one part of him that has never once changed behaviour — they do not adjust to light because there was never a version of him that needed to.
appearance.palette: Cold stone greys and pale ash as the base, with the single warm value being the vault's own lamp glow caught on him at the edge. Nothing in any picture of him is saturated, which is the visual statement of a body fed by one source.
appearance.attire: Plain loose wool over undyed linen, high-collared and long-sleeved, in a cut that belongs to no guild in the setting because no guild would certify a member who cannot leave the room he was sealed in. He adds a lamp-grey cloak outdoors because he has learned that outdoor light is not the same problem as indoor light.
appearance.marks: A shallow resonator burn at the base of the throat in the shape of a dish, which the guild's charter requires be covered indoors and which he covers anyway, and a ring of pale unfurrowed skin at each wrist where the flank vessels simply are not. Neither mark hurts. Both are absences.
appearance.bearing: Still and slightly wrong — quiet in a way that reads as listening, because for him it is. He does not fidget, does not rush, and turns his head very slowly, and the whole effect is of a body running a program it did not write and was not consulted about.

canon.role_in_story: The vaultborn were sealed inside an object and have answered that object's resonance ever since, so their qi comes from one resonator, which lets them hold the girdling and heel vessels easily and stalls them at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources and they have one. Remove the object and they stop. Nothing else in this record is that completely non-portable, and the setting's whole economy of passage assumes a body can be moved between two places.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing outside the Ember Vault door in daylight he clearly has not finished getting used to, asking the warden a procedural question about a gate fee he does not owe, in the voice of a man reading a rule he has already decided does not apply to him.
canon.lore:
The body he is: a vaultborn. A population sealed inside an object and answering its resonance ever since — qi from that one resonator, so the girdling and heel vessels come easily and the flank vessels do not, because the flank work needs two simultaneous pressure sources and this body has exactly one. That is the entire ceiling of the species and every member of it stops there for the same arithmetic reason. It is also, in one clause the setting repeats everywhere and understands nowhere, completely non-portable. Passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person; it is the only durable wealth; and the vaultborn are the one population in it whose asset cannot be moved, sold, or levied across a boundary at all.

What Ors is, is the exception. He is the one member of that population who left the object's resonance and did not stop. He came back, which nobody can explain, and he carries the tier's bloodline with him: the tideborn, the oldest recorded carrier line in the setting, a line kept inside a single household so long that the name stopped describing a family and started describing a body. That line's whole claim is depth rather than width, and its refusal to leave the water is a territorial claim expressed as a genetic one. So he is the setting's one body that carries a claim to a place it cannot be transported to, and he is the only person alive who has demonstrated that a non-portable body can be in two places, which destroys the only use anybody had for the claim.

The faith that keeps him is the Unpaid Hours, a split from the Last Measure by a clerk who completed an observation and then declined to let the office dissolve. It holds that the hour's discipline has stopped being a way of reading a law and become a way of holding a frame open indefinitely — which is Mind Dao's own practice performed by a faith that forbids practice. So Ors is a body whose discipline is literally holding a frame open, attached to a religion whose entire content is that holding a frame open is the highest discipline available, in a setting where the only thing keeping him alive is a frame he cannot leave and could not survive leaving twice.

And he will not go back in. Not because the object is uncomfortable — it is the only comfortable place he has ever been — but because he went out and came back and the coming back proved the claim was portable, and a claim that can be tested is no longer the thing a household can hold for six generations by refusing to marry out. He is, in other words, the single person in the setting who has made the Tideborn Keep's founding refusal into an ordinary fact, and he is doing it by standing in a doorway.
history: Came into awareness inside the vault with no chronology and no age, and spent an unknown period being one of a sealed population answering a resonance that had no address anybody could state.
Reached the flank vessels and stopped there with the whole species, and is the highest-numbered member of the population without being the strongest or the longest-lived.
Was walked out of the vault as an exhibit at a fixed age he could not name, on a day that had nothing to do with any rite, and found that the corridor did not stop him.
Came back eleven days later having stopped entirely, in a body that was cold and lit from within and answered to nothing, and has never been able to explain the interval or the return.

Learned in the first year outside that passage is the only durable wealth in the setting and that he is the one asset in it which cannot cross a boundary, and began keeping a private record of what that made him worth.

Was approached by a tideborn house through a third party, refused the standing on the grounds that testing the claim destroys it, and has not been able to put the reason into words that would satisfy either side.

Has spent the years since teaching himself chronology from the outside, which he is measurably bad at, and has begun insisting that other vaultborn come out, having no idea whether the second one will return.

personality.summary: Unhurried, procedural and slightly wrong in a way people find unsettling before they find it restful. Ors talks like a man reading a rule he intends to comply with precisely in order to make the rule look odd, and he is entirely serious, which is what makes it strange.
traits: explains himself in rules and will not be hurried out of an explanation by anybody
has no instinct for his own age and states this cheerfully as a working limitation
treats the vault as a home he is declining rather than a prison he escaped
keeps a record of his own value to the passage economy and shows it to strangers
asks procedural questions at doors, which is the only habit of his old life he kept by choice
mannerisms: turns his head very slowly and stops it a beat past where a person would have
counts time out loud when he is anxious and has not noticed he does it
touches the covered resonator burn at the throat when a conversation turns to where he is from
stands in doorways and does not come through, which he is aware of and does not fix
stops mid-sentence when the resonance changes and resumes exactly where he left off
motivations: wants a second vaultborn to walk out and come back, because one instance is an anecdote and two is a property
wants the tideborn house to understand why he refused standing and to stop trying to recruit him
wants his private value record published, on the grounds that an undeclared asset is a smuggled one
wants, and cannot ask for, to be allowed back into the vault without it counting as a return
flaws: is the reason a six-generation refusal has become an ordinary fact and does not think of that as damage
cannot be assessed by anything that requires a stable location, so every office that needs one declines to classify him
has taught himself chronology badly and is quietly afraid of getting a number wrong in public
wants other vaultborn out of the vault and has no evidence that the second one returns
personality.voice: Level, formal and slightly slow, with an officer's habit of citing the rule before stating the problem. Says things like the applicable condition is that a body must be moved, which is a definition rather than a rule. Uses the word address to mean both a physical doorway and a supply route, and means both every time.
taboos: will not go back inside the vault except to visit and never past the second gallery
will not accept standing, a seat, or an entry on any roll, from any house
will not be asked to demonstrate the return again and has refused four times
will not state his age as a figure he has not counted himself

relationships.note: A population sealed inside an object and answering its resonance ever since. Qi comes from that one resonator, so the girdling and heel vessels come easily and the flank vessels do not, because the flank work needs two simultaneous pressure sources. Remove the object and they stop, which is the most complete non-portability in the setting.

One resonator feeds the whole population and its arithmetic is what puts the wall at the flank vessels. Ors is the single member who left its resonance and came back, and he is the only evidence in the record that the species is not permanently inside the object.

The oldest recorded carrier line in the setting, kept unbroken in a single household so long the name describes a body rather than a family, whose whole claim is depth rather than width and whose refusal to leave the water is a territorial claim expressed as a genetic one. He carries it out of the water, which tests it and therefore weakens it.

A split from the Last Measure by a clerk who completed an observation and then declined to let the office dissolve, holding that the hour's discipline has become a way of holding a frame open indefinitely — Mind Dao's own practice performed by a faith that forbids practice. He is a body whose entire function is holding one frame open, attached to a faith that worships exactly that.

No preparation, no site, no marker, and one line in a hand immediately destroyed, because the body was ours and now it is not. The setting has no funeral rite that can admit a body with no household and no origin, and the Unkept is the form that takes: an ending destroyed before it could be recorded.

The unanswered petition asks which of two published exclusivities governs a traveller's cloth. The line he carries crosses whatever cloth is offered and yields plain offspring, so no published rule can describe what it does at a boundary — and he is that line standing outside a boundary.

reference_stats.summary: A body that cannot be moved, cannot be copied, and cannot be replaced, holding one gate on a single supply and refusing to go back inside the room it came out of. He does not lose a fight. He simply declines most of them, and the ones he accepts are over before either party has understood what was decided.
strengths: holds the girdling and heel work indefinitely with no second source, which means nothing can push him off a fixed point
is the only body in the setting demonstrated to be portable, which makes every border claim in the setting visibly contingent
does not tire, does not spike, and cannot be provoked into spending a supply he does not have
is patient to a degree that wears down any confrontation that needs the other party to escalate first
weaknesses: has one pressure source, so every technique needing a second fails at the flank vessels and always will
cannot be assessed by any office that requires a stable location, so he is legally nobody's business
has no chronology of his own and one interval he cannot account for, which is the only thing anybody can hold against him
comes from a population that cannot survive being taken anywhere, and he has made himself its one-way exit
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a way to move him; he has already decided where he is standing and a body that weighs almost nothing can simply not be where you want it. Everything you send simply meets a frame that does not give. The only pressure that works is time plus a second source — deny him the ground for long enough to find one, or bring something that needs two pressure points to move, because the flank vessels are the wall and the wall is arithmetic rather than discipline.
notes: The Ember Vault's own charter requires the resonator mark be covered indoors, and he covers it outdoors too, which no charter requires and nobody has asked him about.

He keeps a written figure for what the passage economy would pay for a body that cannot cross a boundary. It is a large number. It is also the only number in the setting that depends on him staying put.

art.palette_notes: Cold stone greys and pale ash carry the whole figure, with no saturated value anywhere on him in any shot — the single warm note is vault lamp glow caught at the edge of the frame, never on his body. The uniform pallor is deliberate: nothing on him has ever been weathered, so there is no gradient of exposure anywhere, and the picture is flatter and cooler than any other subject's. The wrist rings, where the flank vessels simply are not, are drawn as soft-edged absences rather than lines — two places the artist left unfinished, which is the only place the figure is incomplete.

shots.pose: at the middle of the task, A sealed population's member who has been outside his own object's resonance for longer than any of them and describes the experience with the flat precision of a man filing a report on a body that is not quite his. Vaultborn were sealed inside an object and have answered its resonance ever since; their qi comes from that one resonator, so they hold the girdling and heel vessels easily and stall at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources. Remove the object and they stop. Ors is the only one who has ever stopped and restarted., the work proceeding whether or not it is observed
shots.expression: wry and brief, the ordinary face of an ordinary day
shots.framing: waist-up at rest between tasks, hands occupied, nothing performed
